title: Dense integer-lattice restriction for condensed ell-adic derived invariants
statement:
Fix a prime $\ell$, an algebraic closure $\Omega$ of $\mathbf Q_\ell$ with its extended norm topology, and a finite intermediate field $E$. For $F=E,\Omega$, put $C_F(S)=C(S,F)$, using all continuous maps on profinite sets [def-sfb-continuous-map-condensed-ring]. For a finite-dimensional norm-topological $E$-vector space $V$, put $V_F(S)=C(S,F\otimes_E V)$ with the finite-dimensional product norm topology. For a topological group $J$, write $\mathcal A_F(J)$ for internal $C_F$-modules [sk-def-sfb-module-objects] with an action of the condensed group $S\mapsto C(S,J)$; invariants are the equalizer imposing that action to be trivial, and $R\Gamma_J$ is their ordinary total right derived functor in $D(\operatorname{Mod}_{C_F})$ [def-weil-abstract-derived-category].

Let $r\geq0$, let $L=\mathbf Z_\ell^r$ with its inverse-limit topology, and let $D=\mathbf Z^r$ with the discrete topology. The homomorphism $\iota:D\to L$ sends the $i$th standard integer basis vector to $1$ in the $i$th $\mathbf Z_\ell$ factor. Let $V$ have a continuous $E$-linear $L$-action. Restriction of actions along $\iota$ and the inclusion of invariant objects induce the canonical derived restriction morphism
$$b_F:R\Gamma_L(V_F)\longrightarrow R\Gamma_D(\operatorname{Res}_\iota V_F).$$
This is an isomorphism in $D(\operatorname{Mod}_{C_F})$. Its degree-zero map is the identity after identifying $L$-invariants and $D$-invariants. The morphism is natural in continuous equivariant $E$-linear maps of $V$. For $E\to\Omega$ [def-sfb-continuous-map-condensed-ring-map], the square formed by $b_E$, $\operatorname{Res}b_\Omega$ and the canonical derived coefficient maps induced by $v\mapsto1\otimes v$ commutes. The coefficient maps use the natural equality of invariants with scalar restriction. For $r=0$ the comparison is the identity $V_F[0]$.
